The proposal addresses:

- Candidate direction: commits terminal_report at death with the three exit reasons, never the sentinel; collects same-attempt partials before pristine relaunch removal; supervisor log survives abandonment as bounded tail; drain closure exercised not re-specified; horizon stays backstop; kill -9 legal; conformance suite extension with new S-rule; batch grain delivery with two independent signals.

Now let me check consistency with decisions:

D0001: vocabulary. The proposal uses "Lane Supervisor" (admitted in C11), "Driver", "dispatch", "spool", "terminal_report", "Lane". Check for banned terms: "workflow" — I don't see it used. Let me scan... "the same durable commit discipline (fsync-then-rename) the spool already trusts for work submissions" — fine. No "workflow", no "Operator", no "Meta-Operator". Good.

D0003: artifact kinds. The proposal is an L1 Proposal. Forbidden content for proposals: per D0003.C4, each kind declares forbidden content — designs carry no sequencing; plans never relitigate designs; work graphs carry no prose rationale. For proposals, the proposal-generation pass contract postconditions (referenced in the proposal itself) say no architectural commitments, interface definitions, or implementation sequencing. The proposal explicitly declares those as non-goals/constraints. Does the proposal itself violate this? It mentions `internal/spool/closure.go`, `ScanClose` — but that's referencing the existing delivered drain half, which is factual context from the target state itself (the target state names internal/spool/closure.go, ScanClose). It mentions "fsync-then-rename spool discipline" — that's from the target state clause text. It mentions "a new S-rule exercising a real supervised lane" — the target state itself says "proven by an extension of the supervision conformance suite (an S-rule exercising a real supervised lane...)". So these are restatements of the predicate, not new interface commitments.

One potential issue: the "Whole-tree-check atomicity" constraint says "every Go source change this delivery makes must live inside exactly one code packet that compiles and passes those whole-tree checks standalone on the anchored base... Documentation, catalog, and policy-check changes are separate packets that depend on — and are serialized after — that one code packet." Is this sequencing? It's packet-grain structuring, which arguably is work-graph territory (L4). But the proposal says it's "binding, inherited from the intent statement" — i.e., it's a constraint flowing down from L0, not a decision made at proposal level. Constraints inherited from higher levels are appropriate in a proposal. Hmm, but does specifying "code packet first and dependent packets following" constitute implementation sequencing that belongs to the work graph? This is a gray area. The proposal frames it as a constraint on delivery shape, not a sequencing decision. D0003.C3: "a pass never introduces a decision belonging to a higher level" — wait, higher level means... each lowering level removes a named ambiguity class; a pass never introduces a decision belonging to a higher level. So a proposal (L1) shouldn't make design (L2) decisions. Packet structure is L4 (work graph). The constraint says the delivery "must not collapse the delivery into a single subject-grain change-set; the batch shape above, with the code packet first and dependent packets following, is the required split." This is arguably dictating work-graph structure at proposal level. But it's framed as inherited from the intent statement (L0), which is upstream of the proposal — constraints from L0 flow down through all levels. If the intent statement binds whole-tree-check atomicity, then restating it is fine. This is at most a minor finding — the proposal could be clearer that it's restating an inherited constraint rather than deciding packet structure. Actually, it does say "binding, inherited from the intent statement". So it's disclosed. I'd call this not a finding, or a minor one at most.

Let me check the evaluator coverage: the target state's evaluator has 6 nodes: product-dual-signal, delivery-batch-integrated, guard-emits-at-death, guard-collect-before-discard, guard-horizon-backstop, guard-drain-closure. The target state says: "the packet MUST name the registered check set stalls-guards in its acceptance_checks (binding under acceptance-checks-bind@1)" — wait, in the predicate text at the top: "Delivery earns the anchored funnel (conjuncts force a Verified close) and the packet MUST name the registered check set stalls-guards in its acceptance_checks (binding under acceptance-checks-bind@1)." So trl2-guards is the new set containing four guards (three new trl-* plus the shared drain one). The proposal correctly names trl2-guards and treats exit-report-prompt-abandonment as not to be amended. Consistent.

Check the proposal's claim about "two independent admitted signals (mechanical check-set pass and the conformance-suite extension)". The evaluator's signal_rule: d0010-dual-signal-exact-target, minimum_independent_reports: 2. The proposal says the two signals are "mechanical check-set pass and the conformance-suite proof". At proposal level this is fine.

Clause: supervisor-commits-at-death — proposal matches, including "never the upcast-only unobserved sentinel".

Clause: partials-collect-before-discard — proposal: "collects same-attempt on-disk outputs as admitted evidence before the pristine relaunch removal runs, so a collected partial never outlives its own attempt and never fabricates a result its invocation did not produce." Clause: drain-closes-promptly — proposal: exercised, not re-specified. The proposal treats it as standing. Fine.

Clause: delivery-earns-its-own-signals — "with the trl2 guards executing inside both" signals. The proposal says "carrying the two independent admitted signals (mechanical check-set pass and the conformance-suite extension) the target state's evaluator requires". It says "the two independent signals (mechanical check-set pass and conformance-suite proof) must both be mechanically applicable and admitted in this request's context". It doesn't explicitly restate "trl2 guards executing inside both". That's a restatement nuance; the clause requires the guards to execute inside both signals. The proposal's characterization of the two signals as "mechanical check-set pass" and "conformance-suite extension" — if the check-set pass is one signal, then the guards execute inside it by definition. The conformance-suite extension (S-rule) would be the second signal. Do the trl2 guards execute inside the conformance suite signal? The S-rule exercises emission end-to-end; the guards (emits-at-death, collect-before-discard, horizon-backstop, drain-closure) presumably are checked by the conformance suite. This is design-level detail. At proposal stage, the proposal commits to satisfying the evaluator as declared. Minor at most.

Now check: does the proposal introduce anything contradicting D0005? E.g., "No packet may claim a subject-grain self-certifying rebuild" — consistent with D0003.C6 (build never self-certifies) and the batch-shape amendment.

Potential issues to consider as findings:

1. The proposal's "Whole-tree-check atomicity" constraint dictates packet structure (one code packet, docs/catalog packets serialized after). This edges toward work-graph (L4) content in an L1 proposal. However, it's declared as inherited from the intent statement, and the target state amendment itself forced the batch shape. The named forbidden contents listed in D0003.C4: "designs carry no sequencing; plans never relitigate designs; work graphs carry no prose rationale; every packet anchors to a plan element". Proposals aren't listed there, but the proposal-generation pass contract's postconditions (which the proposal cites) forbid implementation sequencing at proposal stage. But since it's inherited from L0 (intent statement) and from the target state's evaluator amendment (batch shape), restating inherited binding constraints is not "introducing" a decision. I'll consider this a minor finding at most, or not a finding. Actually, I think it's defensible as-is; the proposal explicitly disclaims interface/sequencing commitments in non-goals and constraints. I could record a minor finding noting the tension and suggesting the design/work-graph stages treat the atomicity constraint as the binding source. That's a fair minor finding.

The candidate direction's "exercised, not re-specified" resolves it, but the non-goal wording could be misread by downstream stages as forbidding fresh in-context drain-guard evidence.
